messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: `capacity_exhaustion.inference-queue-prod` (P1) — queue depth and processing backlog exceeded thresholds. Auto-escalation to oncall and platform.
PagerDuty: Alert details: queue_depth=12034 (>8000), avg_processing_latency=6.2s, pending_work_items=11k. Link: https://pagerduty.example/incident/INC12345. Runbook: runbook://inference/queue-backlog
Sam: ack — I'm oncall. Starting triage now. @Priya @Jordan on infra side please. Any quick visibility from Grafana?
Priya: pulling dashboards. Queue spike started ~03:17 UTC, steep rise over 3m. 95p latency climbed to 12s. Autoscaler metrics show `scale_events=0` and `pending_pods=0` for the HPA/ASG loop — requests queued but no new nodes accepted.
Priya: grafana snippet:
```
inference.queue.depth  -> 12034
autoscaler.requests.pending -> 0
nodepool.free_capacity -> 0
kube_pod_pending{reason="Unschedulable"} -> 86
```
Jordan: seeing repeated failures from the cloud provisioning API: `QuotaExceeded` and `InsufficientCapacity`. Karpenter requests are being rejected with 403/LimitExceeded. Cloud provider tickets show nodepool at soft quota.
Jordan: sample controller log:
```
E0315 03:18:22 scale.go:142] provisioning failed: CannotProvision: quota exceeded for instance type a100.xlarge in region us-west-2
```
Amy: quick ask — do we have warm spare capacity? If not, we should fallback to lower-cost model variants to preserve latency for critical endpoints.
Sam: immediate mitigation plan:
  1) Manual scale deployment worker replicas where possible to use existing nodes (`kubectl scale`).
  2) If pods stay Pending due to schedulability, shift traffic away from heavy pipelines to lighter variants (route via router config).
  3) Open cloud quota request and contact infra to fast-track capacity.
Sam: executing manual scale (attempting quick wins):
```
# bump replicas for inference-worker-prod
kubectl -n prod scale deployment inference-worker --replicas=12
kubectl get pods -n prod | grep inference-worker | wc -l
```
Sam: result -> pods created but many are `ContainerCreating` then `Pending`. Kube events show `0/8 nodes available: Insufficient gpu`.
Priya: confirmed: nodepool has no GPUs available. Scaling the deployment won't help until nodes spin up. We need extra nodes or preemptive fallback.
Jordan: I'm opening an urgent quota increase with cloud support (ticket CS-87654) and also asking infra slack channel to approve emergency burst pool. Link to ticket: https://cloud.example/support/CS-87654
PagerDuty: Escalation: alert escalated to Platform Lead (cc: @Jordan). Next escalation in 8 minutes if unresolved.
Amy: while cloud responds — switch routing rule for `generate-v1` -> `generate-v1-lite` for non-SLAs. Patch to router:
```
# temp route
PATCH /routes/generate-v1
set backend -> generate-v1-lite
add header x-fallback: auto
```
Amy: I'll push the rule, should cut heavy GPU usage by ~60% but increases cost on lite infra.
Sam: Amy pushed route at 03:24 UTC. Observing traffic shift. Early metrics: queue depth falling to ~7.8k, 95p latency to ~8s.
Priya: good, but customer-facing error rate for /v1/generate still at ~1.8% (spikes for large-context requests). Note: customers X & Y reported degraded experience via support.
Sam: logging incident-annot: customer-impact=true; customers_impacted=["Xcorp","Yapps"]; severity=high.
Jordan: cloud support replied — they can approve quota but ETA ~45m for new nodes to be provisioned. They've recommended increasing regional quota and offered to spin up temporary burst nodes in a paired AZ.
Sam: next steps:
  - Keep fallback routing active (Amy)
  - Jordan continues quota escalation + infra contact (Jordan)
  - Priya monitor queue/latency and try to drain KV cache to speed cold starts (Priya)
  - I'll coordinate customer comms and update PD timeline every 10m (Sam)
PagerDuty: Note: alert will remain open until queue_depth < 2000 for 5m and no Pending pods. Automatic notifications in 10m.
Priya: ran KV cache flush for a subset of prefixes to reduce cold init time:
```
curl -X POST https://ops-api/kvcache/flush -d '{"prefix":"/models/gpt-large"}'
```
Priya: initial improvement: avg init time down ~0.9s.
Sam: manual scale re-attempt after partial capacity freed:
```
kubectl -n prod scale deployment inference-worker --replicas=8
kubectl rollout status deploy/inference-worker -n prod
```
Sam: rollout completing — ~6 new pods Running, queue depth trending down to 5.1k. Still above target but better.
Jordan: cloud confirmed temporary burst nodes will be available in ~22m. I've attached contact and ticket in infra channel. If burst comes up we can autoscale back to normal.
Amy: infra channel acked and will keep the burst nodes warm for 30m after traffic normalizes.
Sam: updating PD with current status and estimated recovery: "Partial mitigations in place (fallback routing + manual scale). Expected stabilization in ~20-30m once burst nodes attach. Customer impact ongoing for large-batch jobs."
Sam: assigning follow-ups: postmortem owner @Priya, mitigation notes @Jordan, customer comms @Sam.
Priya: taking postmortem. I'll capture timeline + thresholds and recommend pre-warming policy for heavy-batch lanes.
Sam: handing off to next oncall @Priya at 04:00 PT. I'll remain watch on-call for 20m in case of regression. :thumbsup:
PagerDuty: Alert acknowledged by Sam. Monitoring continues.
